title: PRD: Degradation and acceptance gates for model quantization regressions
creator: Asha Patel
description: Translate the postmortem findings from the February quantization rollout incident into concrete PRD requirements. Define degradation contracts, automated acceptance gates, observability signals, and rollout/rollback criteria specifically for model quantization changes (new quantized kernels, conversion pipelines, or variant swaps). Goal is to prevent silent quality regressions and ensure measurable, verifiable safety checks are run before and after any quantization-related change in hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: A1: PRD specifies a minimum set of regression tests (embedding similarity, n-gram overlap, prompt-specific evals) that must run in CI and in-the-wild canary for every quantization change.

A2: Define SLO degradation thresholds tied to token-level and application-level metrics (e.g., embedding cosine drop > 0.05, answer correctness drop > 3%) that trigger automatic circuit-breaker and rollback actions.
A3: Instrument KV-cache and prefix-caching verification to ensure quantized paths do not induce cache invalidations; include synthetic cold-start and KV-regeneration checks in PR runs.

A4: Rollout plan includes staged canary (1%, 10%, 50%) with automated quality gates and a mandatory 24-hour observation window before broad rollout; failure in any gate stops rollout and opens incident runbook.

A5: PRD contains a structured fallback policy: if quantized variant fails verification, traffic routes to nearest compatible fallback (float32/alternate-quant) with <200ms routing latency degradation SLA and documented customer notification flow.

A6: Operational playbook and verification checklist embedded in PRD with links to dashboards, synthetic checks, and the runbook page; runbook must include steps for hotfix, rollback, and post-rollback verification.
A7: Console exposes per-tenant quantization change history and per-model quality deltas; at least 90 days of retention for regressions related to quantization.

A8: Security and private-deployments section specifies that quantization testing in Private mode must be runnable offline with local evaluation harness and signed artifacts to prevent binary tampering.
A9: All acceptance criteria must have corresponding automated checks (CI/CD jobs, canary monitors) and owners listed in the PRD before work moves to implementation.
A10: UX/PM acceptance: rollout UX for Dedicated/Private includes explicit opt-in for experimental quantized variants and clear customer-facing impact notes in the Console before enabling.
A11: Example test vectors and baseline scores for top 10 customer-facing prompts are included in the PRD and stored in the evals repo referenced by the implementation tickets.
